key_insight: R² Flow makes LLM agents improve themselves by alternately training on a shared-state execution graph, verifying edits, and updating a skill library recursively.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical framework for building more reliable self-improving agent systems that can reuse, revise, and transfer skills across tasks and executors.
method: Merge histories that differ only by the order of independent steps into a shared-state orchestration graph.
Use flow-share readout plus signed utility ranking to separate frequent skill use from genuinely beneficial skills.
Apply independent verification and a residual-variance plateau to decide when and how to commit library edits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved task accuracy and library-edit precision across question answering, mathematical reasoning, interactive decision making, and code generation, with transfer across executors.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate verification and stable shared-state graph construction, so performance may be sensitive to executor assumptions and edit-trigger tuning.
paper_title: R$^2$ Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution
